newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng rallies to new record close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng rallies to new record close.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index rallied to a new record close on Monday, ignoring calls for consolidation as optimism about the property sector drove property stocks sharply higher, boosting the overall tone.
The Hang Seng index closed on a gain of 153.43 points at 13,042.80 after reaching an all-time intra-day high at 13,094.42. Turnover was HK$8.26 billion compared to HK$7.98 billion on Friday.
"It seems like there is no resistance," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research. "I think the general market sentiment is turning very bullish."
Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas, said investors considered Friday's 115.43-point drop in the Hang Seng index as a buying opportunity. "People are buying on every dip," he said.
"Property is again under the spotlight because property prices recently continued to move up," said Mak.
Shares in Sun Hung Kai Properties led property sector gains.
The stock rose HK$2.75 to HK$93.25, with investors particularly encouraged by a strong response to the company's sale on Saturday of 528 flats at its Tuen Mun development in the New Territories.
Shares in Cheung Kong rose HK$0.75 to HK$67.00 and Henderson Land closed HK$1.00 higher at HK$72.25. Hysan Development advanced HK$0.85 to HK$28.30 and New World Development rose HK$0.50 to HK$47.00.

However, Great Eagle Holdings bucked the trend, closing down HK$0.70 at HK$28.20. The company said it was buying the 365-room Sheraton Tower Southgate Hotel in Melbourne, Australia, from insurer Transport Accident Commission for A$119 million.
"Most sectors performed quite well today," said Henry Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Research. He pointed to strength in the conglomerates, particularly Swire Pacific.
"People are buying market laggards at the monent. Swire Pacific is definitely a laggard," said Lui.
Mak said the Hang Seng index was set to move higher still.
"We have definitely cut through 13,000. It probably will continue," he said. "People are not worried about valuation - just momentum."
Shares in Shanghai Industrial rose HK$1.15 to HK$22.25. The company said on Monday that it had made progress in talks relating to planned acquisitions.
